teaser.en: Clouds of white flowers cover this small coastal tree, a quiet relative of the hibiscus and cotton.

summary.en: *Mbwale* is a small coastal tree or shrub with heart-shaped leaves and clusters of white flowers. Like other Dombeyas it gives fibre and poles.

about.en: *Mbwale* is a small tree or shrub with soft, heart-shaped leaves. It flowers in dense clusters of small white blossoms, which can cover the crown. It belongs to the mallow family, which also includes hibiscus and cotton.

where.en: It grows on coastal forest edges, in wooded grassland and in bushland. It is most noticeable when flowering.

uses.en: Dombeyas are generally used for their tough bark fibre, for tying and rope, and for poles, and *mbwale* is used in similar ways.

names.en: The Digo and Swahili name is *mbwale*. It is recorded in ICRAF's handbook under a related species, *Dombeya rotundifolia*, so the name may cover more than one Dombeya. No English common name has been recorded for *Dombeya taylorii*.

reason.en: Grewia, another bush shrub of the mallow family
